newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends higher, cold forecasts supportive.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends higher, cold forecasts supportive.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures closed slightly higher in all months, with gains in new-crop July attributed to forecasts for possible crop damaging cold weather this week in the Plains, traders said.
Late commercial buying in May wheat erased losses and the contract closed up two cents at $4.26-1/4 per bushel.
One trader said local forecasts had crop-damaging cold from Kansas to the Texas Panhandle Thursday and Friday.
Cargill led buying with 3.7 million bushels of July. Benson Quinn was active buying 1.5 million each of May and July, and selling 2.5 million July.
KCBT wheat closed up 2-1/2 to one cent a bushel with actively traded July settling up 1-1/4 at $3.96-1/4.
Estimated volume Wednesday was 27.385 million bushels, with 17.415 million in July.
